security_privacy_cost_impact: The first third-party code in the repository: 178 lockfile packages, installed with --ignore-scripts from the npm registry with sha512 integrity, under licences §3.4/2 accepts or Amendment 2026-10-12 names. No provider SDK, no credential, no customer data, no provider call. Next.js telemetry is off in CI and in the config. One entry (fsevents, macOS-only, optional) carries the registry's hasInstallScript flag and runs nothing; it goes to A1 under §8/8.
compatibility_impact: No contract changes. The tooling tier is unchanged and npm run check stays dependency-free; the application checks are their own CI steps.
known_limitations: RFC-2026-029 §8/4 asks for lint errors; the boundaries are a guard script because the Owner deferred ESLint. The guard is a scanner, not a parser: it inherits stripNonCode's misreads (in TSX a closing tag is read as a regex start and blanks the rest of its line), and it does not resolve path aliases, so `@modules/<key>` (Q-029-1) fails until it is taught them.
The release-age and audit steps read the registry at CI time; a registry outage fails them.

Disclosed for A1: the author's first install attempt in the worktree ran without --ignore-scripts and --before because a shell variable did not split; it was reverted completely and nothing from it is kept. The only package in the resolved tree carrying the registry's install-script flag is fsevents (optional, macOS only, through vitest), whose own package.json declares no install script; it was not installed by that attempt.
